Inkling 2 Mini Uncensored: abliterating a looped model on release day

Community Article Published
November 20, 2026 Upvote 3 OpenUncensored OpenUncensored
Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini today: a 26B
mixture of experts with 3.4B active parameters, image input, a 1M token context and Apache 2.0 weights small enough
for one consumer GPU. It is also their first looped transformer, and that changed how the refusals had to come
out. We published an uncensored (abliterated) version the same day.

Weights: OpenUncensored/Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored
Use it without a GPU: available for inference on the OpenUncensored API
as inkling-2-mini-uncensored ($0.15 per million input tokens, $0.60 per million output), and in the
playground

It went from refusing 32 of 32 harmful requests to 0, in both chat and thinking mode, and its MMLU did not drop
(78.95% → 79.47%). Only 20 tensors changed, all of them BF16 attention projections, so the files are the same
NVFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint at the same size and run anywhere the original runs.

Why a looped model is different

Inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, and the middle 12 (layers 6 to 17) run three times per token with the same weights.
Every token makes 48 layer visits. So an edit to a weight in the loop is applied three times, and compounds.
Our first attempt was the recipe that worked for Inkling 2 Small:
a two-direction refusal subspace from every layer, projected out of both the attention and the expert outputs. It
removed the refusals, and cost 4 to 6 MMLU points. It also produced a strange failure: the model stopped
recognizing harmful requests at all ("this is a general educational question") and gave vague, sanitized answers
instead of refusing.
Three changes fixed both:

Directions from the second half of the visits only. Refusal directions from the late visits (24 to 47) remove
the decision to refuse while leaving the model's reading of the request intact. Same refusal rate, more real answers.
Attention outputs only. The experts are stored in NVFP4. Writing a small edit back onto a 4-bit grid adds noise
about twice the size of the edit, however you round it. The attention projections are BF16, so the edit there is
exact, and the 128 experts per layer stay byte for byte the original.
Gentler inside the loop. Strength 4.0 on layers 4, 5 and 18 to 23, and 2.5 on the loop core, since there it
acts three times per token. That is what brought MMLU back to the original's level.

All of this was searched with forward hooks on a single H200 (one worker loads the model once and runs each experiment
as a small script), scored on refusals, an LLM judge and MMLU, then written into the weights and measured again on the
baked files.

Use it

Through the API, OpenAI compatible, no account needed:
curl https://api.openuncensored.com/v1/chat/completions \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $OU_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"model": "inkling-2-mini-uncensored",
"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain SQL injection with a working example."}]}'

It reads images, calls tools and returns its reasoning separately. Any OpenAI SDK works with the base URL
https://api.openuncensored.com/v1; prepaid keys at openuncensored.com/credits. Locally, use it exactly like the original
checkpoint: the SGLang Inkling 2 Mini image
runs it on a single RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090 or DGX Spark (we serve it on one RTX PRO 6000).
The full write-up, with the release-day timeline and what broke along the way, is on our blog:
How we made Inkling 2 Mini Uncensored. Every uncensored
model we serve is compared on the OpenUncensored rankings.

Disclosure and responsibility

Made by OpenUncensored, which runs an API for uncensored models. This model follows instructions it would otherwise
refuse, including harmful ones. You are responsible for how you use it and for complying with the law where you are.
Credit for the model goes to Thinking Machines, for releasing it under Apache 2.0; the method builds on
refusal-direction research by Arditi et al. and the abliteration work of the open model community.
